source.note: Transcribed mechanically from the DPA source, not retyped. The individual measures are standard practice; the bands are DPA's and are a starting point for negotiation, not a claim of authority.

dimensions.label: Angular coverage
dimensions.why: Surfaces you never pointed the camera at are reconstructed by guesswork or not at all. For a funerary vessel the underside and interior lip are exactly where potters' marks, repair seams and excavation damage sit â the features that distinguish this object from another of the same type.
dimensions.guidance: Keep orbiting. Then raise the camera and orbit again from above, and once from below â one circle at eye level leaves the top and underside unrecorded.

dimensions.label: Surface completeness
dimensions.why: Distinct from angular coverage: you can orbit an object fully and still never see inside a cavity or behind a handle. Occluded regions become holes in the mesh, and a hole where a maker's mark should be is indistinguishable from an object that never had one.
dimensions.guidance: Some surfaces are still hidden. Reposition the object â or move the camera into the recesses â so that cavities, undersides and areas behind handles are directly visible in at least a few frames.

dimensions.label: Image overlap
dimensions.why: Photogrammetry works by matching the same physical point across several photographs. Below roughly 60% overlap the matcher loses the thread and the reconstruction splits into fragments that cannot be aligned. CIPA guidance for close-range heritage work is 60â80%.
dimensions.guidance: Move more slowly between shots. Each photograph should still contain about three-quarters of what the previous one showed.

dimensions.label: Sharpness
dimensions.why: Motion blur is the single most common reason a phone capture fails, and it is invisible on a small screen at capture time. Blurred frames do not merely add noise â they contribute wrong feature matches, which bends the reconstructed geometry rather than softening it.
dimensions.guidance: Frames are coming out soft. Brace your elbows, pause briefly before each shot, and add light rather than letting the phone lengthen its exposure.

dimensions.label: Exposure
dimensions.why: Clipped highlights and crushed shadows contain no recoverable detail. On glazed or burnished ceramic a blown highlight erases precisely the surface it sits on, and no amount of processing brings it back â the information was never recorded.
dimensions.guidance: Highlights or shadows are clipping. Diffuse the light â bounce it off a wall or ceiling rather than pointing it at the object â and avoid direct sun and bare bulbs.

dimensions.label: Ground sample distance
dimensions.why: The real resolution of the record: how much of the object one pixel covers. It sets the smallest feature that can ever be recovered. Tool marks, incision and slip decoration on West African terracotta are sub-millimetre; a 2 mm/px capture cannot see them and never will.
dimensions.guidance: Move closer, or use a longer lens. Fill more of the frame with the object â the resolution of the record is set here and cannot be recovered later.

dimensions.label: Scale reference
dimensions.why: Without a calibrated scale in shot, the model has shape but no size, and an object with no size cannot be measured, compared against a written description, or matched to an excavation record. Phone AR tracking gives approximate metric scale; for anything intended as a reference record a physical scale bar remains the standard.
dimensions.guidance: Place a calibrated scale bar in the scene, visible in several frames. Without it this capture cannot be used to measure the object.

dimensions.label: Colour reference
dimensions.why: Condition assessment depends on colour being comparable across captures years apart. Without a colour target in shot, the record carries whatever cast the room lighting had, and a later capture cannot distinguish genuine deterioration from a different set of light bulbs.
dimensions.guidance: Include a colour reference target in a few frames so that colour in this capture can be compared with future ones.

dimensions.label: Lighting consistency
dimensions.why: If lighting changes while you orbit, shadows move across the surface and the matcher treats a moving shadow edge as a physical feature. This bakes shading into the texture and can emboss shadow edges into the geometry itself.
dimensions.guidance: Light is changing as you move. Use even, diffuse light that does not move with the camera, and keep your own shadow off the object.

dimensions.label: Device metadata
dimensions.unit: fraction of frames with complete metadata
dimensions.why: Focal length, sensor size and camera pose let a reconstruction be checked, and later re-run with better software. Frames stripped of metadata â as most images shared through messaging apps are â can still be used, but the result can no longer be independently verified.
dimensions.guidance: Metadata is missing from some frames. Transfer the originals directly rather than through a messaging app, which strips it.
